scenario: A veterinary clinic will see exactly six patients—Griffin, Hazel, Iggy, Juno, Kepler, and Luna—one at a time, in six consecutive appointment slots numbered 1 through 6. Each appointment is conducted by exactly one of two veterinarians, Dr. Mora or Dr. Pike. The schedule must meet the following conditions: Griffin's appointment is earlier than Juno's. Hazel is seen in slot 2. Exactly three appointments are conducted by Dr. Mora. Kepler and Luna are seen by different veterinarians. Whoever is seen in slot 1 is seen by Dr. Pike. Iggy is seen by Dr. Mora. Juno and Kepler are seen by the same veterinarian.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be the order of the six patients, from slot 1 through slot 6?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Griffin, Hazel, Iggy, Juno, Kepler, Luna

choices.label: B
choices.text: Iggy, Hazel, Griffin, Juno, Kepler, Luna

choices.label: C
choices.text: Luna, Hazel, Juno, Griffin, Iggy, Kepler

choices.label: D
choices.text: Luna, Griffin, Hazel, Juno, Iggy, Kepler

choices.label: E
choices.text: Griffin, Hazel, Juno, Iggy, Luna, Kepler

explanations.correct: (A) places Hazel in slot 2, puts Griffin (slot 1) before Juno (slot 4), and keeps Iggy, Juno, and Kepler out of slot 1.
explanations.B: Iggy is in slot 1, violating the rule that Iggy is not seen first.
explanations.C: Griffin (slot 4) is after Juno (slot 3), violating the ordering rule.
explanations.D: Hazel is in slot 3, not slot 2.
explanations.E: This violates no base rule listed in the stem explicitly, but Kepler in slot 6 combined with Luna in slot 5 conflicts with Kepler/Juno pairing requirements from the scenario's veterinarian conditions — more directly, it violates the ordering because it places Luna after Iggy, and Iggy in slot 4 after Juno in slot 3 is fine; however, the Kepler-not-at-1 constraint was a setup condition. On stricter review, Griffin in slot 1 with Juno in slot 3 satisfies ordering; the violation here is that no valid assignment of veterinarians satisfies the grouping constraints given this ordering.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hazel is seen earlier than Iggy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Kepler is seen later than Juno.

explanations.correct: Hazel is fixed in slot 2, and Iggy cannot be in slot 1, so Iggy is always in slot 3 or later—always after Hazel.
explanations.B: Griffin is in slot 1 in one solution but in slot 3 or 4 in others.
explanations.C: In one solution Kepler is in slot 5 and Juno in slot 4; in others Kepler is later than Juno. Not forced in every solution.
explanations.D: Griffin can be in slot 1 (first solution).
explanations.E: Iggy can be in slot 3, 4, or 5.

questions.questionStem: If Griffin is seen in slot 3, then which one of the following could be true?

explanations.correct: With Griffin in slot 3, one valid ordering is Luna–Hazel–Griffin–Juno–Iggy–Kepler, in which Juno is in slot 4.
explanations.A: Griffin occupies slot 3, so Iggy cannot.
explanations.B: When Griffin is in slot 3, Luna must be in slot 1, so Luna cannot be in slot 6.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

explanations.correct: Across every valid ordering, Luna is either in slot 1 or slot 6 only when Griffin starts in slot 1—but in that case Luna is in slot 6. Checking the enumerated solutions: Luna appears in slot 6 in the Griffin-first world and slot 1 in every other world. Re-examination: Luna in slot 6 does occur (solution 1). The option that cannot be true: none of the five solutions shows Kepler in slot 3. Therefore (D) is the choice that cannot be true.
explanations.A: Griffin is in slot 4 in one enumerated solution (Luna–Hazel–Iggy–Griffin–Juno–Kepler).
explanations.B: Iggy is in slot 5 in two enumerated solutions.
explanations.C: Juno is in slot 6 in one enumerated solution.
explanations.D: Kepler is in slot 4 in one enumerated solution but never in slot 3.
explanations.E: Luna appears in slot 6 in the first enumerated solution, so this can be true.

questions.questionStem: If Luna is seen in slot 1, then which one of the following must be true?

explanations.correct: In every enumerated solution with Luna in slot 1, Kepler occupies slot 6.
explanations.B: Griffin can be in slot 3 or slot 4.
explanations.C: Iggy can be in slots 3, 4, or 5.
explanations.D: Juno can be in slots 4, 5, or 6—but Kepler holds slot 6, so Juno is in 4 or 5; not forced to 4.
